source_title: Dundee United fan views on 2-2 draw with Celtic - BBC
source_excerpt:
We asked for your thoughts on the 2-2 draw at Celtic that extended Dundee United's unbeaten run to six games.
Kieran: Never thought I would be saying I am gutted with a point at Celtic Park but what a performance from the team going from strength to strength. Glad to see we didn't sit back by choice and credit needs to go to Jim Goodwin for that. Zac Sapsford is now looking like the goalscorer we know he is capable of. The run of form we are on is incredible, long may that continue.
Lee: Disappointed not to get the win but a draw is still an excellent result. We played lots of good stuff, particularly in the first half. Zidane Iqbal and Dylan Tait were outstanding.
Mierse: The fact we are disappointed not to have taken all three points is an indicator of how much we have improved this season. The tackle on Sapsford only getting a yellow card is yet another example of the different standard of refereeing you have to endure when you play against one of the Glasgow teams.
Ian: Heading in the right direction. Bert Esselink reborn, Iqbal superb, but Goodwin doesn't half make some strange substitutions. Anyway a valuable point.
EmeraldIsleArab: In the end a fair result, but United will rue their missed chances. Lachie Rose and Abdoulaye Yoro in particular could've taken all three points, but of course we'll settle for the away draw at Parkhead.
Lee: United can be proud of their classy display. With Iqbal, Tait and Lyall Cameron they currently have the best midfield in the league. In-form Sapsford is now scoring the goals we all knew he could. With better efforts in front of goal and a different refereeing decision, United would have had all three points. The Celtic player should have been sent off for the crunching tackle on Sapsford that left the player wincing. That would have changed the game.
